claims.text: A nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy-alloy film can be deposited by DC magnetron sputtering.
The proposed coating can be deposited onto a CoCrFeNi substrate as a coherent nanocrystalline film.
The coating will contain an optimized concentration of oxide-forming elements.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi suffers increasing friction and wear as temperature approaches 800 °C.
Heating and sliding will produce fine, uniformly distributed, spinel-like oxide precipitates at the coating surface and grain boundaries.
The oxide phase formed by the coating will remain stable and lubricious at high temperatures.
At low temperature, a dense nanostructured coating reduces asperity contact and wear.
At elevated temperature, controlled tribo-oxidation forms an in-situ lubricious layer that protects the underlying alloy.
Nanocrystalline strengthening and the protective oxide film together will lower friction and wear.
Relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi, coated samples will have lower coefficient of friction at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
Relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi, coated samples will have a lower wear rate at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
An AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 alloy exhibited decreasing average coefficient of friction with increasing temperature and reduced wear depth at 800 °C.
The intervention is expected to be effective only under moderate-load sliding in ambient air.
Extreme loads or substantially different atmospheres may change oxide-formation kinetics and tribological performance.
The coated and uncoated CoCrFeNi samples will be compared under identical load and sliding-speed conditions from room temperature to 800 °C in ambient air.
Coefficient of friction, wear volume or depth, microstructure, chemistry, and phase identity will be measured.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction exceeding 20% in both friction and wear at every temperature will falsify the hypothesis.
Absence of the expected lubricious oxide after high-temperature exposure will falsify the hypothesis.
